_note: The arithmetic behind `capture.element` and `capture.screen` (parity/F11-capture.md). Rasterising is platform work and is deliberately not pinned; what IS pinned is the part that silently disagrees between renderers if each writes its own: the format fold, how `scale` resolves, and exactly what pixel size a point size becomes. A share card asked for at 1200x630 must come out at 1200x630 everywhere, and a 20000x20000 request must be refused BEFORE anything tries to allocate it, which is the difference between an error and a crash.

budget._note: Roughly a 6300x6300 square, or 8000x5000. Larger than any share card, poster or receipt, and far below where a phone dies allocating the bitmap. The guard runs on the computed pixel size, so a modest point size at scale 8 trips it just as a huge point size at scale 1 does.

formats.name: the default is png, because transparency is the common case
case is not part of the vocabulary
gif is not a screenshot format

quality.name: a percent is read as a percent, because everyone gets this wrong once
one is one, not one percent

scale.name: an omitted scale is the device scale
the word device is the device scale
an empty string is the device scale
an explicit one is one, whatever the screen is
a numeric string is a number
a device scale of zero falls back to one
an absurd scale is refused before the budget has to catch it
a word that is not `device` is refused

pixels.name: an Open Graph card at scale one is exactly the requested size
a fractional point size rounds per axis, half away from zero
a half scale halves both axes
a one-point view at 1x is still a pixel
a view that has not been laid out yet has no size
a sub-pixel result is not a capture
the 20000 square that would OOM the device is refused
a modest view at an extreme scale trips the same guard
right at the budget is allowed
one pixel past the budget is not

invariants._note: Properties an implementation must hold that arithmetic cannot express. Each facet asserts them in its own tests; they live here so the three renderers cannot drift on what the promise IS.
invariants.transparentByDefault: with no `background`, a png capture keeps the subtree's own transparency; a jpeg, which has no alpha, composites onto white and says nothing, because a jpeg with a black background where the caller expected white is the bug this line exists to prevent
invariants.videoSurfaceIsNotBlack: an Android subtree containing a SurfaceView or TextureView (a video, a map, a camera preview) is captured with PixelCopy rather than View.draw. View.draw produces a BLACK RECTANGLE for those, silently, and that is the defect in every Android screenshot library. iOS has no equivalent split and uses one path
invariants.refIsSurfaceScoped: a `ref` names an element within one surface; the same name on two mounted surfaces resolves to the one the calling context belongs to, and a ref that names nothing is `unknown_ref` rather than a blank image
invariants.notRenderedIsDistinct: a ref that EXISTS but is not currently laid out (a screen below the top of the stack, a collapsed branch) is `not_rendered`, not `unknown_ref`: the caller's mistake is different and so is the fix
invariants.screenIsOurWindow: `capture.screen` captures the app's own window and nothing else. It cannot see another app, the status bar owned by the system, or content behind a system overlay
